The dry trade-wind regime has remained for the Marianas and looks to
continue for the next few days, so isolated showers and mostly cloudy
skies are expected for tonight, becoming partly cloudy Friday 
morning. The northeasterly trades will continue easing up through 
Friday night before increasing the following day. Model guidance 
continues the drier trend for the Marianas through the next several 
days before a potential shift in overall weather conditions over the 
weekend. As of now, models still show a wetter pattern with a slight
chance of thunderstorms preemptively arriving on Guam first before 
spreading northward through the rest of the Marianas. However, 
uncertainty is high as models struggle to agree on the timing, 
location, and speed of a tropical disturbance that could form in 
central Micronesia and travel westward, bringing said weather 
conditions to the region. Satellite imagery does not indicate the 
development of a tropical disturbance in central Micronesia, so 
confidence will remain low until such a system emerges. We will 
continue to monitor and communicate as the weekend nears.

Marine...
Buoy and altimetry data supports a decrease in the easterly trade 
swell, with combined seas of 5 to 7 expected for the coastal waters 
of the Marianas, becoming 4 to 6 feet by the weekend. There is a 
moderate risk of rip currents along north- and east-facing reefs that
is expected to linger throughout the rest of the week. Looking ahead
at next week, swells may rise, increasing surf and combined seas once
again, but unlikely to reach hazardous levels. The sea state will 
continue to be monitored as next week nears.

Eastern Micronesia...
The leading edge of the Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) interacting
with the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) remains the primary 
driver for weather across eastern Micronesia. Extensive heavy showers
and some thunderstorms are expected to continue at Pohnpei through
Friday, followed by a brief and slight decrease in shower coverage. 
Showers and thunderstorms will again peak during the weekend as an 
ITCZ surge continues building from Pohnpei to the Marshalls as 
trade-wind flow continues to bulk against the NET and associated 
developing disturbance, followed by a disintegration in the 
southeasterly component that will push the ITCZ back toward the 
central Pacific by early next week. This backbuilding will bring 
gusty, heavy and intense showers to Majuro before the weekend, with 
some near gale-force gusts expected near the heaviest showers. As the
aforementioned disturbance heads further west and/or northwest, 
showers and thunderstorms will return to a more patchy coverage 
across the region, but a dry spell is not likely to develop as the 
primary convergence zone remains across all three islands.

Combined seas of 4 to 6 feet near Pohnpei and Kosrae, and 5 to 7 
feet near Majuro, are expected to taper down a foot over the coming 
days, to then remain as such for the rest of the forecast period as 
trade swell remains moderate.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite observations show isolated showers over the western half of
the region and scattered to numerous showers over the eastern half of
the region. Altimetry shows combined seas between 4 and 6 feet.

A relative lull is ongoing across Yap Proper and Palau. For Palau 
and Yap, weather conditions look to be in and out of an active phase 
through much of the week with 30 to 50 percent PoPs through 
Tuesday. As we head into next week, a monsoon tail looks to develop 
across the region first at Palau then later at Yap Proper, bringing 
increased shower activity. Additionally, a tropical disturbance may 
reside within or just north of the region next week. This would help 
enhance rainfall across Palau and Yap in the extended range. 
Uncertainty remains high on the location or strength of any potential
tropical disturbance next week, but there is medium confidence for 
increased rainfall, either due to direct impacts of a tropical 
disturbance or from the monsoon tail that forms south of it.

Across Chuuk State, tonight showers were reduced to high-end 
scattered showers. Shower coverage is anticipated to increase to 
numerous Friday, due to the convergence from the monsoon-like trough
to the west, the NET to the south, and the ITCZ to the east meeting 
across Chuuk State. As this convergence comes together, low-level 
vorticity will likely begin to consolidate over Chuuk State as the 
early stages of a tropical disturbance begins to form. However, the 
timing of when exactly this disturbance is expected to form is still 
in question. Widespread locally heavy rainfall is expected Friday 
night through Sunday night for Chuuk, as the tropical disturbance 
shifts west and shifts the inflow band over Chuuk. Showers and 
thunderstorm coverage will slowly decrease starting Monday, but an 
active pattern looks to remain.

Marine conditions are between 4 and 6 feet and look to stay benign
through the weekend. S
